name: HR
description: Workers, positions, departments, employment contracts, compensation, leave, reviews, skills and locations.
purpose: Build a people-operations graph from offer letters, contracts, org charts, leave records and review forms, so that reporting lines, contract terms, pay and skills can be queried in one place.
scope: In scope: workers (employees and contractors), positions, organizational units, employment contracts, compensation components, leave periods, performance reviews, skills and work locations. Out of scope: payroll calculation, tax and benefits administration, and recruiting pipelines.
stories: As an HR business partner I want each worker linked to their position, unit, manager and location so that I can produce an accurate org chart.
As a workforce planner I want positions linked to the skills they require and workers to the skills they hold so that I can find skill gaps and internal candidates.
As a people-operations analyst I want fixed-term contract end dates and leave periods per worker so that I can plan renewals and cover.
cqs: Which position does each worker hold, and in which department or team does that position sit?
Who does each worker report to?
Which units are sub-units of a given department?
Which workers are on fixed-term contracts ending before a given date?
What base salary, bonus and allowances does each contract provide, with amount, currency and pay frequency?
Which workers have leave periods overlapping a given date range, and of which leave type?
What overall rating did a worker receive in their most recent performance review, and who reviewed them?
Which skills does a position require that its current holder does not have?
Which workers are based at a given work location?
What are each employee's id, hire date and contracted weekly hours?
